prompt:
Use case: style-transfer, a tightly constrained surface-simplification edit.
Image 1 is the Twin Hills scene to edit. Image 2 is the approved quiet broad matte rendering target. Keep image 1's landscape framing, exact terrain layout, two main facing hill masses, stepped grassy summit clearings, ALL six empty fenced clearings in their current positions, connected paths, wooden stairs, winding central blue stream, both bridges, waterfall, forest borders and distant sky. Do not add, remove, move, crop or redesign any of those structural elements. Keep the same 1672 x 941 opaque landscape canvas.
Change ONLY surface rendering to the calmer broad chunky treatment of image 2. Make ochre paths broad clean matte connected shapes: remove at least 85 percent of scattered tiny gravel marks, small color flecks and irregular speckled fragments. A few large purposeful stones are enough. Make grassy terraces continuous quiet olive-green planes, with only a few large grouped shrubs at the edges; remove the dense scattered little foliage dots. Simplify rock faces into fewer large clean slate planes, while preserving the complete cliff silhouettes and terrace heights. Pines keep their silhouettes but use larger solid foliage masses. Water stays clearly blue and navigable but uses fewer large flowing bands. Preserve bold stable dark contours and warm/cool separation. This should feel hand-painted, chunky and deliberately simplified rather than intricate, realistic or mottled. Show large calm surface areas throughout the center and on both hills. Keep all architectural/geographic logic intact. No people, armies, directional labels, villages, emblems or new story event. No text, watermark, border or transparency.
